artifacts.summary: Confirms Defects 1-3 live exactly as described in orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh; finds Defect 4's premise moot (roadmap-integration.sh --prune is now a deprecated no-op alias for --regenerate, which already renders wholly from state.json); finds the Territory Note's 'three other open records' stale by one (task 391 completed and archived 2026-11-11, leaving only tasks 558 and 562 as current co-declarers of conclusion-stage.md); recommends an additive joint-batch render, a multi-option loop bounded by the shared MAX_PROBE_INVOCATIONS budget, an approval-gated --write-edges invocation at Step 7, and a documentation-only disposition for Defect 4.

memory_candidates.content: agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/roadmap-integration.sh's --prune flag was converted into a deprecated no-op alias for --regenerate once --regenerate began rendering ## Next/## Open work wholly from specs/state.json (no retention parser reads authored content back out of the file) -- a file built from live state can never accumulate terminal cruft, so there is nothing left for a separate prune pass to remove. Any task reasoning about whether to add/exclude a roadmap prune step should check the script's current header first rather than assuming --prune is still a distinct, more-aggressive operation.

orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh's suggest_from_pool() renders a plain joint /orchestrate batch line ONLY when a probe round has zero file_scope_collision pairs and zero other defers at all; any in_batch collision pair consumes both its members via handled_pair_members[] before the joint-batch branch is ever reached, so a dense ready pool with several collision pairs can return success (any_sequence_rendered=true) having rendered nothing but ordered-sequence lines. Fix shape: render the joint batch for the admitted non-paired remainder ADDITIVELY alongside the sequence lines, not only on a collision-free round.
